Foundations

The decisions everything else is built from.

Foundations · Overview

PrinciplesReady

Six rules every decision in Echo traces back to

Glance, then actDanger, help and mesh status readable at arm's length in under a second.
Dark first, sunlight ready, discreet on demandThree themes for night, glare and not being noticed.
Built for gloves and one hand64dp targets, 12dp gaps, frequent actions in the thumb zone.
Honest by constructionVerified and unverified always look different; no claim the threat model can't back.
Capabilities, not radiosThe UI says what the mesh can do, never which radio does it.
Open, native and offlineBundled open fonts and icons, no dynamic colour, no network.

Patterns

Components combined to get one job done.

Patterns · First run

Onboarding FlowSpec

First launch: what Echo protects and what it doesn't, a map, and the two safety controls

See what's happening around you, without the internet

Phones running Echo pass short reports to each other over radio. No server, no account.

1 · Welcome

What it protects

Group reports, positions and nicknames can be read only by people who joined in person.
Nothing you send carries your name, number or a fixed ID.
Echo keeps no history of where you or others were. Reports disappear when they expire.
No server, no account, no internet except a map download you start.

What it doesn't

Anyone nearby with a radio receiver can tell your phone is running Echo.
Public reports can be fake, and so can their confirmations.
Anyone in your group can read what's sent to it and pass it on.
If your phone is taken unlocked, whoever has it can read your groups until you wipe it.
2 · Protects / doesn't (no skip)

Get a map before you go

The map works offline. Get it now, at home, while you have a connection.

Download a cityOpens your browser · about 40 MB
Load a map fileFrom a friend, no internet needed
3 · Offline map

Two things to know

Discreet modeDarkest screen, no vibration. The eye at the top of the map.
Panic wipeTap, then hold 2 s. Erases everything Echo stored on this phone.
The mesh starts off. Turn it on from the map when you need it.
4 · Discreet mode and wipe

Screens · Settings

What Echo ProtectsSpec

The full honest-claims list, reachable from settings at any time

What Echo protects

It protects

Group reports, positions and nicknames can be read only by people who joined the group in person.
A group report shows which member sent it, and nobody can fake another member's report.
Nothing you send carries your name, number or a fixed ID, and Echo's radio signals change regularly.
Echo keeps no history of where you or others were. Reports disappear when they expire.
A panic wipe makes everything Echo stored unreadable within 2 seconds.
There's no server, no account, and no internet use except a map download you start yourself.
Top
What Echo protects

It doesn't protect

Anyone nearby with a radio receiver can tell your phone is running Echo.
Public reports can be fake, and their confirmations can be faked in bulk.
Anyone in your group can read everything sent to it, see shared positions, and pass them on. If a member's phone is taken, assume the group is exposed and make a new one in person.
If your phone is taken while unlocked, whoever has it can read your groups and post as you until you wipe it or your group makes a new one.
Someone with many receivers may guess roughly where a report was first sent.
Downloading a map reveals the region to your network and the map host.
